## Hosts

| Host | Who uses it |
|---|---|
| `https://api.sandbox-gameye.gameye.net` | Self-serve customers |
| `https://api.production-gameye.gameye.net` | Enterprise customers |

Each host serves its live schema at `/openapi.yaml`, for example `https://api.sandbox-gameye.gameye.net/openapi.yaml`.

Authenticate every client API call with `Authorization: Bearer <token>`. The scope column is the scope the server's handler checks for scoped tokens; where it differs from the spec, the Notes column says so.

## Sessions

| Operation | Method and path | Scope (server-checked) | MCP tool | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `session-run` | `POST /session` | `session:start` | `gameye_launch_session` | Body: `{id?: string, location: string, image: string, env?: object, args?: string[], restart?: boolean, labels?: object, version?: string, ttl?: string, external_id?: string}`.<br>Omitting `version` runs the most recently registered tag for the application (tags ordered by `created_at` descending); there is no tag priority.<br>When a warm pool is enabled for the image and region, request `env`, `args` and `labels` are ignored even when the pool is exhausted (the cold fallback uses the pool's configured env, args and labels). A claimed warm container also ignores `version`, `restart` and `id`: the response `id` is the warm container's name, so always read the session ID from the response. `ttl` and `external_id` are honored.<br>Returns 429 when an organization quota is exceeded, with `X-Quota-Type` and `X-Quota-Limit` headers. Also 402 when a trial quota is exhausted and 420 when no compute is available (retry later).<br>A custom `id` becomes the container name and must be unique across all of Gameye, not only your organization: the reservation checks every container name, including ended sessions, with no organization filter. A 409 on launch followed by a 404 from describe means another organization owns that ID; retry with a fresh one. Derive IDs from a globally unique value (a UUID match ID, or `<game-slug>-<uuid>`). |
| `session-list` | `GET /session` | `session:read` | `gameye_list_sessions` | Query: `all`, `location`, `image`, `tag`, `host`, `playerCount[lt]`, `playerCount[gt]`, `filter[<key>]`, `filterNot[<key>]`.<br>Without `all=true` only running sessions are returned. `location`, `image`, `tag` and `host` are plain exact-match params. `playerCount[lt]` and `playerCount[gt]` are strict. `filter[k]=v` and `filterNot[k]=v` match only the user labels set at launch (the `tags` label), never env or system labels; a session that lacks key `k` fails both, so `filterNot` does not return unlabeled sessions.<br>`labels` holds the raw container labels: `tags` (user labels, JSON), `env` (the full launch environment, JSON) and `gameye` (system labels, JSON). Any token in your organization with `session:read` can read launch env values. Never pass a Gameye API token or long-lived credentials through session env; short-lived per-match values such as a join secret are acceptable. |
| `describe-session` | `GET /session/{id}` | `session:read` | `gameye_describe_session` | `labels` holds the raw container labels: `tags` (user labels, JSON), `env` (the full launch environment, JSON) and `gameye` (system labels, JSON). Any token in your organization with `session:read` can read launch env values. Never pass a Gameye API token or long-lived credentials through session env; short-lived per-match values such as a join secret are acceptable. |
| `session-stop` | `DELETE /session/{id}` | `session:stop` | `gameye_stop_session` |   |

## Players

| Operation | Method and path | Scope (server-checked) | MCP tool | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `join-session` | `PUT /session/player/join` | `session:write` | `gameye_player_join` | Body: `{session: string, players: string[]}`.<br>Server checks `session:write`; the spec declares no security for this operation.<br>Response `players` is every player now in the session (not only the ones just joined) and `count` is its length. Joining is per session ID; an unknown or foreign session returns 404. |
| `leave-session` | `DELETE /session/player/leave` | `session:write` | `gameye_player_leave` | Body: `{session: string, players: string[]}`.<br>Server checks `session:write`; the spec declares no security for this operation.<br>Body must include `session`: the handler decodes the join body `{session, players}` and looks the session up by it, so omitting it returns 404.<br>Response `players` is the players remaining in the session and `count` is its length; `players` is `null` (not `[]`) when the session is empty. |

## Logs and artifacts

| Operation | Method and path | Scope (server-checked) | MCP tool | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `stream-logs` | `GET /logs` | `logs:read` | `gameye_get_logs` | Query: `id` (required), `follow`.<br>`follow` defaults to `true`: the stream stays open until the client disconnects or the request timeout. Pass `follow=false` to get the logs written so far and close. |
| `artifacts` | `GET /artifacts` | `artifact:read` | `gameye_get_artifacts` | Query: `session` (required), `path` (required).<br>Query params are `session` (the session ID, not `id`) and `path` (a path inside the container), both required.<br>Returns an uncompressed tar stream (Docker `CopyFromContainer` output) with `Content-Type: application/octet-stream` and `Content-Disposition: attachment; filename="<session>.tar"`. Do not gunzip. |

## Tokens

| Operation | Method and path | Scope (server-checked) | MCP tool | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `create-token` | `POST /token` | `token:write` | `gameye_create_token` | Body: `{name: string, scopes: string[], expires_after?: string}`.<br>With scoped tokens, requested `scopes` must be a subset of the caller's own scopes (403 otherwise); `webhook:github` is the one scope a `token:write` caller may delegate without holding it. Omitting `expires_after` creates a non-expiring token.<br>Token names are unique per user, but a duplicate `name` returns `500` ("Unable to acquire token."), not 409: the unique-index violation is not mapped to a conflict. Include a unique suffix in every name and do not retry a token-create 500 with the same name.<br>Admin-gated: needs an admin-level scope; the MCP tool is opt-in. |

The `tls` flag on ports is not applied by edit, so ports sent through edit end up with `tls=false`; set TLS ports when creating the application or ask Gameye support.<br>Admin-gated: needs an admin-level scope; the MCP tool is opt-in. |

## Webhooks

Registry webhooks register newly pushed tags with Gameye. Source: `spec/webhook.yaml` (no host serves this spec). They are configured in the registry, not called by an agent, so they have no MCP tool.

| Operation | Method and path | Scope (server-checked) | MCP tool | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `v1-dockerhub-webhook` | `POST /v1/integrations/dockerhub` | `webhook:dockerhub` | none | Basic auth, but only the password is read and authenticated as a token with the `webhook:dockerhub` scope; the username is ignored. Docker Hub webhooks cannot set headers, so put the token in the URL: `https://anything:<TOKEN>@<host>/v1/integrations/dockerhub`. 204 when the tag was registered; 404 when no application uses the repository. |
| `v1-github-webhook` | `POST /v1/integrations/github/{organization_id}` | `webhook:github` | none | No bearer or basic auth: GitHub signs the raw body with HMAC-SHA256 and sends `X-Hub-Signature-256: sha256=<hex>`; the server tries every active `webhook:github` token of the organization in the path as the key. In GitHub set the payload URL to `https://<host>/v1/integrations/github/<organization_id>`, content type `application/json`, the secret to a `webhook:github` token, and select the Packages event. Only `package` events with action `published` for container packages register a tag (204); ping and other events get 200. The route is mounted only where the GitHub integration is enabled. |

Deprecated aliases, do not use in new setups: `POST /dockerhub`.
